messages:
incident-bot: Pager: High error rate (5xx) on /v1/inference in us-west-2. Alert triggered by anomaly detection.

oncall-syd: Picking this up — oncall here. seeing spikes from a set of hostnames: inf-ff-prod-*.

maria: I can run a quick query against request logs to scope affected customers. giving ETA ~10m.

alex: quick note — we also got a storage alarm on s3-access-logs-uswest2 with a surge of GETs around the same time. might be related.

jordan: omg could be creds leak. any evidence of object list/GET from odd IPs?

ops-isaac: looking. initial grep shows a small number of requests from an IP range not allocated to us, hitting a customer-data prefix in a dev bucket.

oncall-syd: Pause any automated sync jobs to that bucket. Can someone rot the prod S3 access keys ASAP if they're still active?

maria: pausing syncs now. running identifier scan for files with user PII (emails/SSNs). returns in progress.

ops-isaac: I rotated the app read keys for the ingestion service and revoked the long-lived token used by the sync job. Keys rotated at 09:12 PT.

alex: thanks isaac. can we snapshot the bucket ACLs and object list for forensic? keep read-only copies.

ops-isaac: snapshotting manifest to internal-sec/forensics/1832754321-manifest.txt and taking read-only export.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2025-1832754321. Severity: P2 (potential data exposure). Pager rotation: syd -> alex -> jordan.

maria: quick scope update: preliminary scan found ~4 objects under customers/customer-123/profile/* that contain email + hashed phone numbers. no SSNs in the objects scanned so far. scanning remaining list (ETA 20m).

jordan: which customers are those? need to prep customer-success and legal.

maria: affected customer ids: customer-123, customer-987 (partial logs), and one deprecated test org.

customer-success-ryan: I can start a private channel with the CS lead for customer-123 and draft an initial heads-up. please add language about extent (we don't know wider scope yet).

legal-ana: tagging in. we need the forensic manifest and list of object keys plus access logs to confirm exposure window before any external notice. preserve chain of custody.

tech-comm-liz: standing by to draft status page and customer email once we have confirmed scope. prefer short-messaging: what happened, who is affected, mitigation actions, and follow-up timeline.

alex: forensic note: I see 12 GETs from 203.0.113.0/24 between 08:58 and 09:07 PT. They requested a prefix that matches customer-123 profile exports.

maria: scan complete: 4 customer-123 objects with emails, 2 customer-987 objects with limited logs (no emails), test org objects contain synthetic data.

legal-ana: Based on current evidence, we should prepare a notification to customer-123 as they have confirmed object access. For other customers, we need more log correlation; do not send broad notices yet.

tech-comm-liz: Draft status page copy (short) — please review: ```We are investigating an incident affecting object access in an S3 bucket in us-west-2. We have rotated credentials, paused sync jobs, and are conducting forensic analysis. A subset of objects for one customer were accessed; we are reaching out to affected customers. Updates will follow.```

oncall-syd: I like that. Add ETA for next update: +3h.

customer-success-ryan: Draft customer email to customer-123 (for review): ```Hi <Name>, We detected unauthorized access to a small number of objects tied to your account in an S3 bucket on <date/time>. The data accessed includes email addresses and hashed phone numbers. We have rotated keys, paused syncs, and are conducting a full forensic review. We will share a detailed update within 72 hours and are available for a call. - Redwood Inference```

legal-ana: tweak: replace "unauthorized access" with "access by an external IP address" for neutrality, and confirm precise timestamp. Also add contact for escalation + dedicated point of contact in CS.

tech-comm-liz: ack. also recommend including remediation steps we took and that passwords/token rotations are not required on their side unless we confirm credential compromise tied to their account.

alex: action items recap: 1) ops to preserve access logs and export to secure evidence bucket (isaac) 2) infra rotate keys (done) 3) remove public ACLs if present (isaac) 4) CS draft and run customer email (ryan + liz) 5) legal sign-off on wording (ana) 6) update status page (liz) 7) prepare incident summary for execs (syd)

ops-isaac: ACL audit shows one object had public-read on a legacy export path from a migration script. revoking public-read now.

maria: correlation shows the GETs match that legacy export path exactly. Likely root cause = migration script accidentally left public ACLs on that prefix. important: not a platform credential compromise but misconfiguration.

legal-ana: that's significant. If confirmed it's misconfig and only that bucket/prefix, we can scope notification to customer-123 and state cause as a misconfiguration. Need final confirm of total object count accessed.

oncall-syd: next update plan: I'll post interim status page copy and internal brief in 30m after we finish log preservation and export.

tech-comm-liz: i'll post status page and set update cadence to every 3 hours until resolved. Draft status line for public page: "Investigating limited exposure of customer data due to S3 object ACL misconfiguration. We have rotated keys and revoked public ACLs. Affected customers are being contacted"

customer-success-ryan: prepping dedicated support thread for customer-123 and scheduling a call. will coordinate on messaging after legal sign-off.

jordan: forensics ask: keep original logs and manifests unchanged, store checksums, note chain-of-custody. I'm taking point on the timeline.

legal-ana: once we have final counts and object keys, I'll advise on whether regulatory disclosure is required (we may need to file depending on EU/UK data residency or PII sensitivity). keep me posted.

ops-isaac: export complete to secure-evidence/INC-1832754321. ACLs revoked. keys rotated.

maria: final scope check: 4 objects accessed, all under the legacy prefix, all tied to customer-123. No other customers found after full scan.

legal-ana: with that confirmation, proceed with targeted customer notification and status page update. I'll review the customer email and provide final edits.

tech-comm-liz: putting this on the status page now. Internal comm to execs in progress — draft in #incidents-private.

oncall-syd: thanks team. final checklist before we close P2 -> P3: confirm CS outreach sent, legal sign-off received, evidence archived, remediation steps documented, post-incident RCA scheduled.

customer-success-ryan: CS outreach scheduled and will go out after legal sign-off (expect in ~20m).

legal-ana: sign-off provided on draft with small wording changes. send when ready.

tech-comm-liz: email sent to customer-123 at 09:48 PT; they acknowledged receipt and requested a call at 10:15 PT. status page updated at 09:50 PT.

oncall-syd: lowering severity to P3 for follow-up and RCA. tagging owners for RCA: ops-isaac, maria, jordan.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2025-1832754321 status changed to: mitigated (P3 follow-up).

maria: thanks all. I'll start the timeline and evidence notes for the RCA.

jordan: I'll coordinate post-mortem and include steps to prevent reintroducing public ACLs in migration scripts.

tech-comm-liz: adding customer communication artifacts to the incident package.

legal-ana: will advise on any regulatory reporting next steps after RCA.

oncall-syd: closing loop here. if anything new appears, re-pager will go out. great job. :thumbsup:
